cf.title: Assorted Win32 error handling fixes (CreateThread, pgwin32_select, pg_usleep)

input.subject: Assorted Win32 error handling fixes (CreateThread, pgwin32_select, pg_usleep)

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived the panel, so nothing stops patches 0003 and 0004 at levels 1a, 1b or 2. Both are small, local fixes to Win32 port code with a stated problem and no new user-facing surface. Confidence is low because nobody has reviewed 0004, and the thread does not say whether elog(FATAL) is safe for every pg_usleep() caller.

brief.title: Win32 error handling fixes in pgwin32_select and pg_usleep
brief.problem: Several Win32 port functions mishandle error returns. The author found them with new analysis tooling. The two CreateThread fixes are already committed, so the open problems are a one-element overflow in the pgwin32_select() events array and pg_usleep() treating WAIT_FAILED as a timeout, which can make retry loops spin.
brief.proposed_design: Patch 0003 sizes the pgwin32_select() events array as 2*FD_SETSIZE + 1 so the signal event fits after full, disjoint read and write fd sets. Patch 0004 makes win32 pg_usleep() handle WAIT_OBJECT_0 and WAIT_TIMEOUT explicitly and call elog(FATAL) on any other result from WaitForSingleObject().
user_visible_surface: pg_usleep() on Windows now raises FATAL when WaitForSingleObject() fails, where it used to return at once.
author_claims: 0003 and 0004 are defensive fixes with no reachable in-core trigger.
0004 changes behavior on the failure path and needs review; 0003 is mechanical.
The series passes the author's GitHub Actions CI run.
Only 0001, now committed, had practical server impact.
brief.thread_state: Heikki Linnakangas committed 0001 and 0002 on 2026-10-15 and said he did not look at 0003 and 0004. Nobody has reviewed 0004 yet, and CFbot reports that the patch needs a rebase.
unclear: The proposal does not say whether FATAL is safe for every pg_usleep() caller, such as postmaster or code running in a signal or critical context.
The proposal does not say whether an elog(FATAL) inside pg_usleep() can recurse or fail when logging is not yet set up.
The proposal does not say whether 0003 and 0004 should be back-patched.
No test or reproduction is offered for either remaining fix.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: Patch 0003 removes a one-element write past the end of the events array in pgwin32_select().

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The entry is tagged Bugfix, and the thread does not say whether 0003 and 0004 should be back-patched.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Is elog(FATAL) safe for every caller of win32 pg_usleep(), including the postmaster and code that runs in a critical section?
Can pg_usleep() run before error reporting is set up, or from inside error reporting, so that the new elog(FATAL) fails or recurses?
Why is FATAL the right response to WAIT_FAILED, compared with a log message followed by a plain Sleep() for the requested time?
Should 0003 and 0004 be back-patched, given that the author says neither has a reachable in-core trigger?
Can pgwin32_select() receive full, disjoint read and write fd sets from any extension or frontend caller, or is 0003 defensive only?

committability.owner_note: Heikki Linnakangas committed 0001 and 0002 in message #3 and said he did not look at 0003 and 0004. They need a committer who knows the Win32 signal emulation and the pg_usleep() callers.
committability.liability: The committer signs for a new FATAL exit in win32 pg_usleep(), which many backend and postmaster paths call. The changed lines are few, but the set of affected callers is large and Windows-only.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted a rebased v2 in message #2 and moved the entry to the next CommitFest. CFbot has reported a needed rebase since 2026-10-15, with no reply in the thread.

priority.reason: The two remaining patches are about 1.3 KB each, touch only src/backend/port/win32, and by the author's account in message #2 have no reachable in-core trigger. 0003 is mechanical; 0004 needs a rebase and a Windows-aware reviewer for the FATAL choice.

provisional_note: No code was read, so the 0003 array arithmetic and the exact 0004 control flow are unchecked. Whether the new FATAL can fire in a context where elog() is unsafe needs the code and the list of pg_usleep() callers.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_usleep for multisecond delays
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch first added a pg_ssleep() wrapper so multisecond sleeps would not need long microsecond constants in pg_usleep() calls. After review it became a WaitLatch()-based sleep function (later pg_msleep()) that takes a wait event and responds to postmaster death and interrupts.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch stayed work in progress, and the visible messages do not show the closing decision. Andres Freund objected that long pg_usleep() sleeps are not interruptible, which moved the design to WaitLatch(). Tom Lane then asked for more call sites, a wait event per caller, and a review of the seconds-as-double API. The author posted a new draft in July 2023 and asked whether to drop interrupt handling, and no updated patch appears after Kyotaro Horiguchi's reply.

precedents_retrieved.title: Restart pg_usleep when interrupted
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a sleep function, later named pg_usleep_non_interruptible, that restarts nanosleep() with the remaining time when a signal interrupts it, and stops once the requested time has passed. Vacuum cost delay would use it so the parallel vacuum leader sleeps the full delay even when parallel workers send it frequent progress messages.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the entry after the thread questioned whether the extra code was worth it. Nathan Bossart noted that interrupts rarely hit a vacuum delay point and that rate-limiting worker progress reports to 1 Hz would remove most of them, and the uninterruptible sleep would make vacuum slower to react to SIGTERM or cancel. CF #5118 would also change how pg_usleep() handles these interrupts, so the author left the question to that work.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Is it really that important to delay with that level of accuracy?

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix Windows network event handling
precedents_retrieved.summary: On Windows, the patch moves socket event handles out of each WaitEventSet into a reference-counted per-socket hash table, and adds its own level-triggered event memory, so the edge-triggered FD_CLOSE event is no longer lost. It also changes simplehash for raw malloc/free and no-OOM behaviour, and would let the graceful socket shutdown on Windows be put back.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The entry was returned with feedback in the 2024-01 commitfest because CFbot showed test failures and no updated version followed. In review, Robert Haas questioned the simplehash changes: whether SH_RAW_FREE is needed, whether the no-OOM change in 0002 is a good idea at all, and why raw malloc/free is used instead of palloc/pfree. The visible messages show no reply to that review.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I wonder whether we really want 0002. It seems like a pretty significant behavior change -- now everybody using simplehash has to worry about whether failure cases are possible.

precedents_retrieved.title: Use WaitLatch for {pre, post}_auth_delay instead of pg_usleep
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch replaces pg_usleep with WaitLatch for the pre_auth_delay and post_auth_delay waits, so a backend sleeping there exits when the postmaster dies. It also adds PreAuthDelay and PostAuthDelay wait events.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane argued that these delays exist only for debugging, so adding cost to connection startup to make them visible is wasted effort, and interruptibility by postmaster signals is of little value too. Michael Paquier agreed to drop the patch and noted that wait events are not visible at SQL level at that stage. Nathan Bossart still supported the WaitLatch change, but the entry was closed as rejected.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I follow the idea of using WaitLatch to ensure that the delays are
interruptible by postmaster signals, but even that isn't worth a
lot given the expected use of these things.

precedents_retrieved.title: Eliminating "Permission denied" errors on stat() (on Windows)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes the Windows stat() replacement (_pgstat64) retry on ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED, as pgwin32_open() already does, so that files in the "delete pending" state do not cause "could not stat file ... Permission denied" errors in functions such as pg_ls_waldir(). It also undoes the _NtQueryInformationFile() handling added in bed90759f and makes pgwin32_open() call the native stat().
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier committed the patch but reverted it the same day because it broke the MinGW buildfarm member fairywren. The author sent a MinGW-compatible version, but Michael said he needed MinGW test infrastructure before looking at it again. The author then withdrew the entry in favor of Thomas Munro's "Check for STATUS_DELETE_PENDING on Windows" patch, which detects the status directly.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think that my patch should be withdrawn in favor of
https://commitfest.postgresql.org/34/3326/ ("Check for
STATUS_DELETE_PENDING on Windows" by Thomas Munro), that use deeper
understanding of the problematic status, not indirect indication of it.

precedents_retrieved.title: Get rid of an extra error for client disconnection on Windows
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Tom Lane, Michael Paquier, Alvaro Herrera
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changed pgwin32_recv so that WSAECONNRESET from WSARecv is returned as EOF, as recv(2) does on Linux. This removes the "could not receive data from client" log message on Windows when a client exits without PQfinish().
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that WSAECONNRESET also covers a host reboot, a disabled network interface and a hard close, so treating it as EOF would hide real errors that should be logged. Michael Paquier and Alvaro Herrera judged that removing one log message did not justify that risk, and Michael Paquier marked the entry rejected.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm fairly concerned that this change would mask real errors that ought
to get logged.

precedents_retrieved.title: Use latch instead of pg_usleep for standby recovery conflicts
precedents_retrieved.summary: Simon Riggs added a CHECK_FOR_INTERRUPTS() call to the standby's wait for recovery conflict resolution, and Michael Paquier then proposed a deeper fix for HEAD. That fix replaces the pg_usleep() in ResolveRecoveryConflictWithVirtualXIDs(), which can sleep up to 1s, with WaitLatch() and a new wait event.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Review found that CHECK_FOR_INTERRUPTS() does nothing in the startup process and that WL_LATCH_SET has no effect because MyLatch is never set there. Michael Paquier then judged that calling HandleStartupProcInterrupts() would reload the GUC context in the middle of replaying a record. He concluded that all conflict code paths should use a latch, and returned the patch with feedback as time ran short.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Calling
HandleStartupProcInterrupts() is actually dangerous I think, because
it would reload the GUC context while replaying a record.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Enable parallel SELECT for "INSERT INTO ... SELECT ..."."
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Enable parallel SELECT for "INSERT INTO ... SELECT ..."."
Reverted commit(s): Doc: Update description for parallel insert reloption.; Add a new GUC and a reloption to enable inserts in parallel-mode.; Improve FK trigger parallel-safety check added by 05c8482f7f.; Enable parallel SELECT for "INSERT INTO ... SELECT ...".; Fix use of relcache TriggerDesc field introduced by commit 05c8482f7f.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
To allow inserts in parallel-mode this feature has to ensure that all the
constraints, triggers, etc. are parallel-safe for the partition hierarchy
which is costly and we need to find a better way to do that. Additionally,
we could have used existing cached information in some cases like indexes,
domains, etc. to determine the parallel-safety.

List of commits reverted, in reverse chronological order:

ed62d3737c Doc: Update description for parallel insert reloption.
c8f78b6161 Add a new GUC and a reloption to enable inserts in parallel-mode.
c5be48f092 Improve FK trigger parallel-safety check added by 05c8482f7f.
e2cda3c20a Fix use of relcache TriggerDesc field introduced by commit 05c8482f7f.
e4e87a32cc Fix valgrind issue in commit 05c8482f7f.
05c8482f7f Enable parallel SELECT for "INSERT INTO ... SELECT ...".

precedents_retrieved.title: Parallel INSERT (INTO ... SELECT ...)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set allows parallel execution of both the INSERT and the SELECT parts of "INSERT INTO ... SELECT ...", with workers inserting tuples themselves; where parallel insert is unsafe (for example foreign keys or ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE), only the SELECT part is parallelised. It changes the planner, executor and parallel-worker code, adds parallel-safety checks on the target table (including partitions, triggers and domains), and adds a GUC and a reloption to control the feature.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Parts of the work, "Parallel SELECT for INSERT" and the related GUC/reloption, were committed during the thread. The remaining patches, which add the parallel INSERT functionality itself, were marked Returned with Feedback because of feedback given on pgsql-committers, which said a lot of work remained. The visible messages do not show the content of that feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
There is a lot of work
to do for this patch as per the feedback given on pgsql-committers
[1].

precedents_retrieved.objection:
In commit 462bd95705a0c23ba0b0ba60a78d32566a0384c1, I changed postgres_fdw
to rely on get_plan_rowmark() instead of get_parse_rowmark().  I still
think that's a good idea in the long run, but as Etsuro Fujita pointed out,
it doesn't work today because planner.c forces PlanRowMarks to have
markType = ROW_MARK_COPY for all foreign tables.  There's no urgent reason

time pressure.

Also, add a regression test case showing what postgres_fdw does with FOR
UPDATE/SHARE.  I'd blithely assumed there was one already, else I'd have
realized yesterday that this code didn't work.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the precedent search returned no earlier proposal with the same or a similar idea. The thread does not point to any earlier discussion of the pgwin32_select() array size or of WAIT_FAILED handling in pg_usleep(), so the prior-attempts angle has nothing to raise.

Neither remaining patch changes SQL syntax, GUCs, catalogs, pg_dump output, psql or the wire protocol. The one behavior change, FATAL instead of an immediate return when WaitForSingleObject() fails inside pg_usleep(), is on an internal failure path that the author says no in-core code can reach. Whether FATAL is safe for every caller is a safety question for another angle.

The remaining patches 0003 and 0004 touch only process-local Win32 code: an in-memory event array in pgwin32_select() and the error path of pg_usleep(). Neither changes on-disk format, WAL, replication, catalogs, the wire protocol or an exported struct or signature, so this angle finds nothing to object to.

Neither remaining patch changes who can do what or what anyone can learn, and no unprivileged user can trigger the failure paths. 0003 removes a one-element overflow on the stack, which helps safety, and the FATAL in 0004 fires only on an internal handle failure that a client cannot cause.

Both remaining patches are small, local fixes in src/backend/port/win32 with no new API, GUC, catalog or hot-path cost, so there is no maintenance or fit objection to raise. Whether elog(FATAL) is safe for every pg_usleep() caller is a safety question for another angle. Committability depends on a Windows-aware committer picking up 0004, since Heikki did not look at it in message #3.

Both remaining patches are bug fixes to internal Win32 port code, so no existing feature, extension or external tool can serve in their place. Patch 0003 corrects an array size in pgwin32_select(), and patch 0004 changes how win32 pg_usleep() handles a failed WaitForSingleObject() call. Neither duplicates an existing mechanism or adds a second way to do one job.

Demand is the wrong test for these fixes. 0003 fixes a one-element array overrun and 0004 adds a missing error check, so neither adds a feature or user-facing surface that needs users; the author's "no reachable in-core trigger" bears on priority and back-patching. Whether FATAL is safe for every pg_usleep() caller is a design question for another angle.
